# Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects identified by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. On completion,
each of these flows can be completed end to end using the keyboard alone, with
no focus traps, no unreachable controls, and consistent visible focus
indicators.

## Scope

- Fix the focus-loss defects in modals used by the four audited flows so that
  keyboard focus is managed correctly through modal open, interaction, and
  close within those flows.
- Make every control in the four audited flows reachable and operable via
  keyboard alone (audit-enumerated unreachable controls).
- Make focus indicators visible and consistent across the four audited flows,
  resolving the inconsistencies called out by the audit.
- Address only the defects enumerated in the audit report for the four audited
  flows; screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require and
  flows outside the four audited ones are out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn,
  model deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed from start to
  finish using only the keyboard, verified by walking each flow end to end.
- **AC2**: No focus traps remain in the audited flows — keyboard users can
  always move into and out of every modal and control group encountered in the
  four flows.
- **AC3**: Every control in the four audited flows is reachable and operable
  by keyboard; the audit's enumerated unreachable-control defects are each
  resolved.
- **AC4**: Focus indicators are visibly present and stylistically consistent
  across all controls in the four audited flows.
- **AC5**: The existing Dashboard build pipeline remains green with the
  changes merged.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P1): The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls — covered by AC1–AC3.
- **HLR-2** (P1): Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows — covered by AC4.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
to reflect the fixed state of the four audited Dashboard flows: the Voluntary
Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) and the product documentation
accessibility statement. Two public-sector customers require an updated,
published conformance statement before renewal, so the published documentation
is a first-class deliverable of this strategy, not an incidental touch-up.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT so its conformance claims for the four audited flows
  (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run
  submission) reflect the completed keyboard-accessibility remediation.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the
  current accessibility state of the audited flows.
- Republish both artifacts through the Red Hat docs content process.
- Technical review of the updated documentation against the implemented
  keyboard-accessibility fixes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: The VPAT's claims for keyboard operability and focus visibility in
  the four audited flows match the implemented, verified behavior.
- **AC2**: The product docs accessibility statement is updated to reflect the
  fixed state of the audited flows.
- **AC3**: Both documents are republished (publicly available at their
  established locations) with the updates live.
- **AC4**: The updated documentation has been technically reviewed against the
  implemented keyboard-accessibility fixes, with review sign-off recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3** (P2): The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review — covered by AC1–AC4.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

Strategy: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows

## Triage Outcome

Full decomposition (not below-threshold, not docs-only): the strategy spans two
components (Dashboard, Documentation) and two architecturally distinct work
streams — Dashboard code remediation and substantive conformance-content
authoring (VPAT + accessibility statement). The multiple-distinct-work-streams
escape condition rules out below-threshold treatment.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 Dashboard keyboard fixes] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 VPAT and accessibility statement]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | The VPAT and accessibility statement describe the fixed state; they must be authored after the keyboard fixes land and must be technically reviewed against them. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Coverage |
|-----|----------|------|----------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Full keyboard operability of the four audited flows (no focus traps, no unreachable controls) |
| HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Consistent visible focus indicators across the audited flows — same component, team, and UI surfaces as HLR-1; bundled |
| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | VPAT and product-docs accessibility statement updated, republished, technically reviewed |

All HLRs covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Decomposition Decisions

- **HLR-1 + HLR-2 bundled into one epic**: both concern the same four audited
  flows on the same component (Dashboard) and team (RHOAI Dashboard). Focus
  indicator consistency is part of the same keyboard-accessibility remediation
  surface; splitting would build the same remediation twice with an artificial
  serialization edge.
- **HLR-3 as a separate `docs-authoring` epic**: VPAT authoring and the
  accessibility statement rewrite are substantive content work (not incidental
  doc touch-ups falling out of the code change), owned by a different team and
  run through the Red Hat docs content process.
- **No Investigation epics**: the strategy's open questions section states
  "None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow." The audit
  report resolves all unknowns; remaining detail (per-control fix approach) is
  implementation detail for the team, not a genuine unknown.
- **docs-authoring priority exception**: HLR-3 is P2, consistent with the
  strategy frontmatter priority `Normal` → P2. The docs epic does not push
  priority onto E001.
- **Component mapping**: `Dashboard` and `Documentation` are both verbatim
  canonical component names from `.context/rhai-components.txt`. Dashboard has
  an architecture context file (stable, owning team RHOAI Dashboard,
  opendatahub-io/odh-dashboard); Documentation has no architecture context
  file but is an established docs-content component in the canonical list —
  no provisioning/onboarding chain applies.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements section. Epic acceptance criteria below were
  derived from the HLRs and problem statement; the docs owning team
  (RHOAI Documentation) is inferred from component ownership conventions, not
  stated in the strategy.
- **External schedule risk (not an AC)**: the customer renewal deadline tied
  to the published VPAT is an external schedule constraint; the docs epic's
  controllable completion point is publication of the reviewed documentation.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing.
